actual_scope: On an equal-weight cycle of any length, does every proper arc meet the touching diameter?
scope_change_reason: Length 8 meets the diameter at every width. The named next step was one deleted vertex on the length-9 width-1 cycle. The same negative sign pattern proves the equality at every length, so the package records that proof.
bottleneck_link: The periodic caller reuses a width-w count. After a contiguous arc is eliminated, the complement bandwidth is the touching diameter, which can be half the cycle. The inverse block identity still holds. Boundary order is untouched.
stop_rule: Stop once the equal-weight sign pattern is proved for every length. Do not change a sign or start a boundary-order Gaussian elimination.
evidence: research/equal-weight-cycle-diameter proves the rim gap and the negative Schur sign. Length 9, width 1, one deleted vertex has entry -1/16 and bandwidth 2. Width 2 has entry -1/64 and bandwidth 4.

open_questions.question: Can one positive off-diagonal entry make a touching pair cancel?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The equality uses a negative in-band sign. A cancellation would be the first host whose circular bandwidth falls short of the touching diameter.
open_questions.first_step: Change the sign of one neighbor entry on the length-9 width-1 cycle, delete the opposite vertex, and compare the rim entry with zero.
open_questions.blocked_by: Only the equal negative host is proved here.
